title: THE SAME MARK ON THE SONS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses also brought Aaron's sons forward and put some of the blood on the lobes of their right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands and on the big toes of their right feet. Then he splashed blood against the sides of the altar." - Lev 8:24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The sons receive the identical marking. Same ear, same thumb, same toe, same blood.

Their garments were simpler than Aaron's. Their duties were narrower. But the consecration was exactly the same.

That is a good picture of the church. There are differences of gift, role, visibility, and responsibility. There is no difference at all in the claim God has on our lives. The volunteer who stacks chairs is consecrated by the same blood as the person who preaches.

Peter says it of all believers: you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's special possession (1 Pet 2:9). Every one of those phrases was originally spoken of Israel as a whole, and Peter applies them to ordinary Christians scattered across Asia Minor — many of them poor, many of them slaves.

If you have sometimes felt that "consecrated to God" is language for missionaries and ministers, read verse 24 again. The sons got the same blood.

Your ear, your hands, your feet. Marked and claimed.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I think of consecration as something for "full-time" Christian workers?
2. What would change if I saw my daily work as priestly service?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You have claimed my life as fully as anyone's. Help me to live today as someone consecrated to You. Amen.
